name: Pseudocertainty Effect
description: When an earlier uncertainty is framed as already resolved, people can treat a later probabilistic outcome as if it were effectively certain, even though the total net probability has not changed. The path to the outcome changes its psychological weight.
design_relevance_note: Useful for multi-step flows, insurance/warranty copy, funnel messaging, risk communication, and staged disclosures: resolving one uncertainty on-screen can make a later conditional outcome feel more guaranteed than it really is.
prevalence_note: Named mainly in prospect-theory, policy, and risk-decision writing rather than in ordinary day-to-day UX critique, but still useful in choice-architecture work.

findings.description: In multistage choice problems, preferences shifted as if a later probabilistic outcome were certain once an earlier uncertainty was framed as already resolved, even though the overall net probability was unchanged. This is the core pseudocertainty pattern described in Tversky and Kahneman's framing work.
findings.source_title: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice
